ai.description: This frog reaches 20–25 mm. It is brown with a distinct dark interorbital bar and a pale snout. Key features include a granular belly and a characteristic, high-pitched, insect-like call.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes bobingeri* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored X-shaped marking on its dorsum, which is absent in most similar bush frog species.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes bobingeri* inhabits the evergreen forests and high-altitude shola grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Raorchestes bobingeri is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden in dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes bobingeri* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in leaf axils or moss.
ai.distributionRemarks: Raorchestes bobingeri is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting the high-altitude evergreen forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes bobingeri* consists of a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps heard primarily from vegetation in evergreen forest habitats.
